rows.solution:
Homologous organs have the **same basic structure and origin** but perform **different functions**: the forelimbs of whales, bats, cheetahs and humans share the same bones (humerus, radius, ulna, carpals, metacarpals and phalanges) yet are used for swimming, flying, running and grasping.

Such organs show that related animals, starting from a common ancestor, have been modified in different directions to suit different needs. This is **divergent evolution**. Analogous organs (similar function, different structure, such as the wings of a butterfly and a bird) are the ones that indicate convergent evolution. So the answer is option (B) Divergent evolution.

rows.stem: Which of the chromosome in a human possesses the least number of genes ?
rows.solution:
The Human Genome Project found that the number of genes differs widely between chromosomes:
- **chromosome 1** carries the most genes (2968);
- the **Y chromosome** carries the fewest (231).

So the answer is option (D) Y-chromosome.

rows.stem:
Given below is a list of some commercially important products in column A, whereas in column B are names of source organisms :
| Column – A | Column – B |
|---|---|
| Bioactive Products | Source Organisms |
| A. Cyclosporin – A | (i) Streptococcus |
| B. Statins | (ii) Trichoderma polysporum |
| C. Streptokinase | (iii) Penicillium notatum |
| D. Penicillin | (iv) Monascus purpureus |
Select the option where the product and their source organisms are correctly matched.
rows.solution:
Match each bioactive product to the microbe that makes it:
- **Cyclosporin A**, the immunosuppressive agent used in organ-transplant patients, is made by the fungus Trichoderma polysporum: A – (ii).
- **Statins**, which lower blood cholesterol, are made by the yeast Monascus purpureus: B – (iv).
- **Streptokinase**, the clot buster, is made by the bacterium Streptococcus: C – (i).
- **Penicillin**, the first antibiotic discovered, is made by the mould Penicillium notatum: D – (iii).

So the answer is option (D) A – (ii), B – (iv), C – (i), D – (iii).

rows.stem: What is artificial insemination in ART ? Under what conditions is the person medically advised to go for it ?
rows.solution:
**Artificial insemination (AI)** is an assisted reproductive technique in which **semen collected from the husband or a healthy donor is artificially introduced into the vagina or into the uterus** of the female. When the semen is placed in the uterus it is called intra-uterine insemination (IUI).

A couple is medically advised to go for it when:
- the male partner is **unable to inseminate** the female; or
- the **sperm count in the ejaculate is very low**.

rows.stem: Why does a patient of ADA – deficiency require repeated infusions of genetically engineered lymphocytes ? Suggest a possible permanent remedy.
rows.solution:
- In gene therapy for ADA deficiency, lymphocytes are taken from the patient's blood, grown in culture, given a functional ADA cDNA through a retroviral vector and returned to the patient. These genetically engineered lymphocytes are **not immortal**: they have a limited life span, so as they die the patient needs **periodic infusions** of fresh engineered lymphocytes.
- A **permanent cure** is possible if the gene isolated from **bone marrow cells producing ADA** is introduced into cells at an **early embryonic stage**, so that every cell descended from them carries a working ADA gene.

rows.stem: With reference to flower colour two independent crosses were made, one between true breeding garden pea plants and another between true breeding Antirrhinum plants. Write the phenotypes of their \(\text{F}_1\)-progeny. Justify your answer giving reason.
rows.solution:
**Garden pea (complete dominance).** In pea, violet flower colour is dominant over white.

Parents: violet (PP) \(\times\) white (pp)
Gametes: P and p
\(\text{F}_1\): Pp, **all violet** flowered.

Although the \(\text{F}_1\) carries the white allele, it does not show, because the dominant allele P completely masks the recessive allele p. This is **complete dominance**, and the \(\text{F}_1\) looks exactly like the dominant parent.

**Antirrhinum, snapdragon (incomplete dominance).**

Parents: red (RR) \(\times\) white (rr)
Gametes: R and r
\(\text{F}_1\): Rr, **all pink** flowered.

Here the \(\text{F}_1\) resembles neither parent but has an intermediate colour, because the allele R is not completely dominant over r. This is **incomplete dominance**. (Selfing the pink \(\text{F}_1\) gives red, pink and white in the ratio 1 : 2 : 1, so the phenotypic and genotypic ratios are the same.)

The marking scheme labels the pea parent "violet" and the \(\text{F}_1\) "purple"; they are the same colour, which NCERT calls violet.

rows.stem:
The schematic representation as above is showing the linking of two DNA fragments.
(a) Name 'A' and 'B' fragments.
(b) Write the 'palindrom' recognised by EcoRI.
(c) Where does EcoRI cut the palindrome ? Write the events followed thereafter to form a recombinant DNA.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED: two DNA pieces labelled ''A' DNA' and ''B' DNA', each drawn as a double strand ending in a block of shaded bars with a letter C on the end bar, an arrow carrying the bars of 'B' over to the gap beside the bars of 'A', and the word EcoRI below; the drawing is the only place 'A' and 'B' are defined, so it is needed for part (a). Which piece is the vector and which the foreign DNA is not stated in the drawing either. Page idx 14.
rows.solution:
(a) In the schematic, **'A' DNA is the vector DNA** (for example a plasmid) and **'B' DNA is the foreign DNA**, the desired or alien DNA that is to be inserted into the vector.

(b) The palindrome recognised by EcoRI reads the same on both strands when each is read in the \(5' \rightarrow 3'\) direction:

5' G A A T T C 3'
3' C T T A A G 5'

(c) EcoRI cuts each strand **between the bases G and A** of this palindrome (5'-G AATTC-3'). Because the cuts on the two strands are a little away from the centre, they leave short single-stranded overhangs (AATT) called **sticky ends**. When the vector ('A' DNA) and the foreign DNA ('B' DNA) are both cut with the same enzyme, their sticky ends are complementary, so they pair by hydrogen bonding, and the enzyme **DNA ligase** then joins the sugar-phosphate backbones, forming the **recombinant DNA**.

rows.stem:
How do the following organisms act as bio-fertilisers ? Explain.
(a) Mycorrhiza
(b) Anabaena
(c) Rhizobium
rows.solution:
(a) **Mycorrhiza** is a symbiotic association of a fungus (for example Glomus) with the roots of a higher plant. The fungal partner **absorbs phosphorus from the soil and passes it on to the plant**. Mycorrhizal plants also show resistance to root-borne pathogens, tolerance to salinity and drought, and better overall growth.

(b) **Anabaena** is a free-living cyanobacterium of aquatic and terrestrial environments that **fixes atmospheric nitrogen**. In paddy fields it serves as an important biofertiliser, and it also **adds organic matter to the soil**, increasing its fertility.

(c) **Rhizobium** lives symbiotically in the **root nodules of leguminous plants** and **fixes atmospheric nitrogen into organic forms** that the plant uses as a nutrient.

rows.stem:
(i) Explain the following phases in the menstrual cycle of a human female :
(1) Menstruation
(2) Follicular phase
(3) Luteal phase
(ii) 'A proper understanding of the menstrual cycle can help immensely in family planning.' Do you agree with the statement ? Provide reasons for your answer.
rows.solution:
(i)
- **Menstruation (menstrual phase):** the cycle starts with menstrual flow, which lasts for **3 to 5 days**. It is caused by the **breakdown of the endometrial lining of the uterus and its blood vessels**, which leaves the body as a liquid. Menstruation occurs only when the released ovum is **not fertilised**.
- **Follicular phase (proliferative phase):** the primary follicles in the ovary grow into a fully mature **Graafian follicle**, and at the same time the **endometrium regenerates** by proliferation. These changes are brought about by rising levels of the pituitary hormones (LH and FSH) and of ovarian estrogens. It ends with ovulation, around the 14th day, when the LH surge makes the Graafian follicle rupture and release the ovum.
- **Luteal phase (secretory phase):** the remaining parts of the Graafian follicle change into the **corpus luteum**, which secretes large amounts of **progesterone**. Progesterone is essential for **maintaining the endometrium**, which is needed for implantation of a fertilised ovum and for the maintenance of pregnancy. If fertilisation does not take place, the corpus luteum degenerates, the endometrium disintegrates and the next menstruation begins.

(ii) **Yes**, the statement is correct. A woman who understands her cycle knows that ovulation occurs around the middle of the cycle, so the chances of fertilisation are very high from about **day 10 to day 17**, the fertile period. In the **periodic abstinence** (natural) method of contraception, the couple avoids coitus during this fertile period, which prevents conception. Knowing the same window also helps a couple who want a child to plan intercourse when conception is most likely.
